diagnostics.title: fetch Response consumed without status check
diagnostics.message: `fetch()` resolves (does not reject) on HTTP 4xx/5xx, so this unchecked body read may treat an HTTP error payload like a successful response. Check `response.ok`/`response.status`, or deliberately handle the API's error payload, before reading the body.
diagnostics.help: Check `response.ok` (or `response.status`) before consuming a `fetch` Response with `.json()`/`.text()`/`.blob()`. `fetch` resolves on HTTP 4xx/5xx, so an unchecked response parses the error body as success or crashes on an always-truthy guard.

diagnostics.title: await inside a loop
diagnostics.message: This makes the for…of loop slow because each await runs one after another, so collect the independent calls & run them together with `await Promise.all(items.map(...))`
diagnostics.help: Collect the items, then use `await Promise.all(items.map(...))` so independent work runs at the same time

diagnostics.title: Array lookup inside a loop
diagnostics.message: This scales poorly because `array.includes()` inside a loop scans the whole list every time. Use a Set for constant-time lookups.
diagnostics.help: Use a `Set` or `Map` when you check for the same items over and over. `Array.includes`/`find` scans the whole list each time

diagnostics.title: Spread copy before sort()
diagnostics.message: This wastes work because [...array].sort() copies the array just to sort it, so use array.toSorted() to sort without the extra copy (ES2023)
diagnostics.help: Use `array.toSorted()` (ES2023) instead of `[...array].sort()` so you sort without copying the array first

diagnostics.help: Upgrade to a version with no known advisories (run `npm audit` to find one), or replace it; update `"form-data": "^4.0.0"` in package.json. If you've reviewed and accepted this package, raise `supplyChain.minScore` (currently 50) or set `supplyChain.severity: "warning"`.
